items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: And eventually I went down to New Jersey and took some lessons with him. But a big influence, one of my favorite drummers of all time.

ctx.x: Well he was around the house quite a bit when I was growing up, because he was friends with my dad. And when he was traveling with the quartet he used to come home to his family and inevitably stop by and see my father, and talk about the road and what was going on and give the latest album to my dad, autographed. And I can remember when he came up with “Rondo a la Turk.” That was something else that — what do you think of this — and you know my father would say, “You’re playing terrible.” Constantly put him

on and they would put one another on constantly, so I was exposed to him. And when he came through, he would ask me, “Well how’s your left hand?” You know, how’s this going, how’s this going, and listen to me a little bit, and forget about it. And he was a task master. And he wanted the student that really wanted it. You couldn’t just have an interest in music, you have to want it, and I wanted it, and I kept coming back to it. And then I asked him, “Well listen to this now.” And eventually I went down to New…
And he had a start with — well Marian McPartland was kind a of big part of his initial career, wasn’t it?
